nowFeed.linkText: Marcus Giamatti, whose late father Bart banned Pete Rose in 1989, told ESPN he opposes the Hall of Fame candidacy of the newly reinstated Rose.  Re: the Hall's "character clause," Giamatti said Rose "didn't show the character to rehab, his actions and attitude stained the game, and it doesn't matter if he only bet on his team to win.  Sportsmanship goes out the window – he bet on the game of baseball.  There's no personal integrity."

nowFeed.linkText: "Reinstating him, even after he died, puts in peril the future & integrity of the game … (it) lets the damage he did to the game become OK," Marcus Giamatti told ESPN, re: the end to Pete Rose's ban that his late father Bart imposed in 1989.  He added that Rose "did nothing to rehabilitate, repent or be remorseful" & his father wouldn't have let him back in, as Rose never "reconfigured his life" – the condition for reinstatement.

nowFeed.linkText: RHP Bobby Miller, who was in the concussion protocol after a 2/20 liner struck his head, is up from Triple-A to start for the Dodgers Wed.  He declined a recent ESPN interview request re: post-injury head protection.  Cap insert manufacturers SST & Unequal told ESPN they aren't aware of any current MLB pitchers wearing their products.  An MLB official said no pitchers are wearing the isoBlox & Half-Cap protective headwear MLB approved years ago.  Such decisions are up to the individual.

nowFeed.linkText: As first reported Tuesday, the Department of Defense removed from its website an article titled "Sports Heroes Who Served: Baseball Great Jackie Robinson Was WWII Soldier."  Robinson's Dodger teammate and fellow Hall of Famer Pee Wee Reese, who was also a military veteran, famously supported Robinson in the face of racist abuse.  On Wednesday, Reese's son Mark told ESPN he is not at all surprised at the news, adding, "How far we have come is being erased, literally."

nowFeed.linkText: In a statement to ESPN, John Dowd, who investigated Pete Rose for MLB in 1989, said of Pres. Trump's newly announced plan to "pardon" Rose: "Our president never lets the facts get in the way of a sound approach and is expert at blaming others."  Dowd, who was Trump's lawyer 7 yrs ago, said Trump can pardon Rose for his tax convictions & that MLB is "not in the pardon business nor does it control admission to the HOF" (Hall of Fame rules prevent admission of players banned from MLB).

nowFeed.linkText: Pres. Trump said late Fri. he'll sign a "complete pardon" of MLB hits leader Pete Rose, who died 9/30 at 83. Ineligible for the Hall of Fame after a lifetime ban for gambling on MLB, Rose served prison time after a guilty plea to tax charges. Trump, who has no authority over MLB or the HoF, didn't say what the pardon would cover, but ripped MLB for not having the "courage or decency" to put Rose in the HoF.  His post (copy/paste): https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/114085325641437111
